### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A02 appeared in about 49 in 100 traces (97 of 200; roughly one occurrence per trace, recurring in about 24 in 100), with its outgoing flow going mainly to A13 (about 42%), A08 (about 17%) and A09 (about 15%). In the later window, A02 is not observed at all: 0 of 200 traces, no occurrences and no outgoing transitions, and every monitored pair containing A02 (for example with A13, A14, A07 or A09) changed from co-occurring in about 24–49 in 100 traces to never co-occurring. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL007, REL008]

- A03 and A14 became much rarer: each appeared in about 49 in 100 traces before and in about 19 in 100 in the later window (97 → 37 traces), and when they do occur they sit later in the trace (A03 mean relative position about 0.37 → 0.51; A14 about 0.49 → 0.61). [OCC002, OCC003, POS002, POS005]

- A10 became more frequent and earlier: about 24 in 100 traces before versus about 46 in 100 in the later window (48 → 92 traces), with its mean relative position moving from about 0.52 to about 0.36. [POS003, DIR007]

- Routing around these activities was redistributed. A08's outgoing flow switched from mostly A10 (about 81%) to mostly A03 (about 69%); A09's switched from mostly A03 (about 35%) to mostly A10 (about 47%); A15's switched from mostly A03 (about 60%) to mostly A10 (about 63%); A14's outgoing converged on A13 (about 76%, versus about 33% to A07 before); A10's outgoing moved from A02 and A13 (about 37% each) to A07 (about 33%) and A11 (about 25%); and A06's outgoing moved from mostly A03 (about 47%) to mostly A10 (about 43%). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR010, DIR011, DIR007, DIR004]

- Pairs not containing A02 also shifted: A03 with A13 and A13 with A14 fell from co-occurring in about 48–49 in 100 traces to about 18–19, while A07 with A10, A09 with A10 and A10 with A13 rose from about 23–24 to about 44–46 in 100. [REL014, REL025, REL017, REL021, REL023]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a structural change removed A02 from the executed process and rerouted the surrounding flow. In the earlier window A02 ran in about half of all traces (97 of 200); in the later window it does not appear in any of the 200 traces, its outgoing transitions are unobserved, and all nine monitored pairs containing A02 changed from regular co-occurrence to none. Alongside this, A03 and A14 are executed in far fewer traces (about 19 in 100, down from about 49) and later within them, while A10 is executed in more traces (about 46 in 100, up from about 24) and earlier, with successors redirected accordingly: A08 now leads mostly to A03 instead of A10; A09, A15 and A06 now lead mostly to A10 instead of A03; and A14 now leads mostly to A13. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, REL001, REL007, OCC002, OCC003, POS003, POS005, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR010, DIR011]

This reading rests on direct and consistent measurements rather than on the number of items: the participation, direction and position indicators agree, and the key counts are substantial (A02: 97 traces before versus 0 after; its outgoing transitions: 202 observed before versus 0 after). The screening also qualified 60 items against roughly 0.67 expected if nothing had changed, and each item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, so the set of differences as a whole is far beyond what an unchanged process would produce. [OCC001, DIR001]

Limitations: zero participation only shows that A02 was not observed; the evidence cannot rule out that the later window covers a different case mix in which A02 is simply never triggered, rather than the activity having been removed. The aggregated profiles also cannot pin down the exact new edge structure, and the many direction, relation and lag items overlap on the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations of one underlying change. [OCC001, DIR002]

Other differences: the distances between consecutive occurrences shifted for several pairs — A03 then A09 now typically sits about 3 steps apart (about 79 in 100) versus 1–2 steps before, A14 then A09 now typically about 2 steps apart (about 83 in 100) versus 1 step before, and A13 to A03 lost its immediate one-step relation — and A11 now occurs somewhat earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.49 → 0.40) with little change in how often it appears. [LAG002, LAG014, LAG009, POS004]

message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- Two windows, 200 traces each.
- Screening: 134 units tested, 60 items qualified, 0.67 expected by chance without change. Control flow family: 134 tested, 60 items, 0.67 expected. So 60 items vs 0.67 expected — the count is many times larger than the chance expectation. This cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past the "insufficient evidence by count" gate.

Now judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Key observations:

OCC001: A02 — before: mean occurrences per trace 1.01, participation 0.485 (about 49 in 100 traces), recurrence support 0.24. After: all zero. Support before 97, after 0. So A02 disappeared entirely from the later window — not observed at all.

OCC002: A03 — before: mean 0.87, participation 0.485, recurrence 0.215. After: mean 0.36, participation 0.185, recurrence 0.1. Decreased. Support 97 → 37.

OCC003: A14 — same numbers as A03: before participation 0.485, after 0.185. Support 97 → 37.

DIR001: A02's outgoing transitions — before has a full profile (A13 0.42, A08 0.17, A09 0.15, etc.), after empty. Support 202 → 0. Consistent with A02 disappearing.

DIR002: A03's outgoing transitions redistributed: before A14 0.74 dominant, A02 0.09, A13 0.07, A09 0.06, A08 0.03, A10 0.006. After: A14 0.74 still, A11 0.08, A10 0.08, A05 0.04, A07 0.06. So A02 edge gone (consistent with A02 disappearing), new edges to A05, A07, A10, A11 appear. Support 174 → 72.

DIR003: A05's outgoing: before A02 0.27, A13 0.29, A08 0.32, A10 0.05, A09 0.07. After: A03 0.16, A13 0.34, A14 0.16, A08 0.18, A09 0.16. A02 edge gone, A03 and A14 appear. Support 41 → 38.

DIR004: A06's outgoing: before A03 0.47, A11 0.29, ... After: A10 0.43, A03 0.10, A11 0.18, A09 0.15... So A03→ down, A10 up. Support 34 → 40.

DIR005: A08's outgoing: before A10 0.81 dominant. After: A03 0.69 dominant. Big shift. Support 105 → 72.

DIR006: A09's outgoing: before A03 0.35, A14 0.25, A11 0.17, A15 0.10. After: A10 0.47, A11 0.14, A15 0.14, A05 0.08, A07 0.12. A03 and A14 gone, A10 dominant. Support 48 → 49.

DIR007: A10's outgoing: before A02 0.37, A13 0.37, A03 0.10. After: A07 0.33, A11 0.25, A13 0.14, A09 0.08, A10 0.05... A02 gone. Support 105 → 184.

DIR008: A11's outgoing: before A03 0.27, A15 0.30, A06 0.18, A02 0.09. After: A15 0.32, A10 0.22, A06 0.22, A09 0.08, A13 0.08. A03 down, A10 up. Support 77 → 92.

DIR009: A13's outgoing: before A02 0.34, A03 0.19, A08 0.17, A09 0.13. After: A09 0.30, A08 0.28, A10 0.20, A11 0.07, A07 0.07. A02 and A03 gone. Support 202 → 164.

DIR010: A14's outgoing: before A07 0.33, A11 0.20, A09 0.08, A13 0.09. After: A13 0.76 dominant. Support 174 → 72.

DIR011: A15's outgoing: before A03 0.60, A11 0.33, A08 0.07. After: A10 0.63, A11 0.17, A13 0.08, A09 0.08, A14 0.04. A03 gone, A10 dominant. Support 43 → 52.

POS001: A02 — before support 0.485, mean position 0.40; after all zero. Consistent with disappearance.

POS002: A03 — support 0.485 → 0.185; mean position 0.37 → 0.51 (later in trace).

POS003: A10 — support 0.24 → 0.46; mean position 0.52 → 0.36 (earlier).

POS004: A11 — support 0.215 → 0.225; mean 0.49 → 0.40.

POS005: A14 — support 0.485 → 0.185; mean 0.49 → 0.61 (later).

REL items: many involve A02. REL001–REL009 all show A02 co-occurring with partners before (co-occurrence 0.13–0.485) and zero after, with B_only and neither up. This is all consistent with A02 disappearing.

REL010–REL026 involve other pairs: A03 with partners — co-occurrence drops (e.g., REL014 A03/A13: 0.485 → 0.185), B_only rises. REL017 A07/A10: co-occurrence 0.23 → 0.445 (up). REL019 A08/A10: co-occurrence 0.24 → 0.185, B_only 0 → 0.275. REL021 A09/A10: co-occurrence 0.235 → 0.45. REL023 A10/A13: co-occurrence 0.24 → 0.46. REL025 A13/A14: co-occurrence 0.485 → 0.185, A_only 0 → 0.275.

LAG items: various lag distribution shifts.

So the picture: A02 was present in about 49 in 100 traces before (mean ~1 occurrence per trace) and is completely absent in the later window (0 in 200 traces). Also A03 and A14 participation dropped from about 49 in 100 to about 19 in 100. A10 participation rose from 24 in 100 to 46 in 100. Many routing shifts: A08 now goes mostly to A03 (was mostly to A10); A09 now goes mostly to A10 (was mostly to A03); A14 now goes mostly to A13 (was spread, mostly A07); A15 now goes mostly to A10 (was mostly A03); A10's outgoing shifted from A02/A13 to A07/A11.

The dominant, direct finding: A02 disappeared entirely. That's a participation change (activity removed / became unobserved). The evidence for this is direct: OCC001 (participation 0.485 → 0.0, support 97 → 0), POS001, DIR001 (outgoing profile empty, support 202 → 0), and all the REL001–REL009 items showing co-occurrence with A02 dropping to zero.

Secondary: A03 and A14 became much less frequent (participation roughly halved from ~49% to ~19%), and occur later in traces when they do occur (mean position up). A10 became more frequent (24% → 46%) and occurs earlier.

Now, what hypothesis does this support? The instructions: "Changes in participation, routing shares or repetition can support a hypothesis that part of the process is executed more often, less often, skipped or repeated differently..." A02 going from ~49% participation to zero is a participation change — the activity was not observed in the later window. That's a hypothesis in its own right: A02 is no longer executed (or no longer observed).

Note the caution: "Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window." So the hypothesis should be phrased as: A02 was no longer observed in the later window — consistent with the activity being removed or skipped in all cases.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" level? Let's check the criteria:

- Count comparison: 60 items vs 0.67 expected — many times larger, so chance can't explain the whole set. Good.
- Directness: OCC001 directly shows A02 participation 0.485 → 0.0 with support 97 → 0. DIR001 shows its outgoing transitions vanished (support 202 → 0). POS001 shows position support 0.485 → 0. REL001–REL009 show co-occurrence with A02 dropping to zero across nine partners. This is direct and highly consistent.
- Competing explanations: Could A02's disappearance be a sampling artifact? With 200 traces and 49% participation before, the probability of zero occurrences in 200 traces if participation stayed at 48.5% is essentially (0.515)^200 ≈ 0 — astronomically small. The empirical strength 0.995 also indicates the difference is unusual for random splits. So the "rare variant appears in one window only" concern doesn't apply here — A02 was common before and totally absent after. The competing explanation of chance sampling is effectively ruled out by the sample size.

However, one caveat: zero participation only means not observed. Also, could the activity have been renamed? We can't rule out relabeling, but we shouldn't speculate. The evidence supports: A02 is no longer part of observed behaviour.

What about the changes to A03, A14, A10 and the routing shifts? Are these part of one hypothesis or separate? The instruction says: state one main hypothesis first and name the activities it involves. If evidence also shows other differences not part of this hypothesis, report under "Other differences:".

The main hypothesis: A02 was removed from the process (no longer executed). Supporting: OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL001–REL009.

But wait — is the A03/A14 decrease and routing redistribution part of the same underlying change? Possibly A02's removal caused rerouting, but we shouldn't speculate about causality chains too much. Actually, the DIR changes show that successors of many activities changed: e.g., A05 no longer goes to A02, A10 no longer goes to A02, A13 no longer goes to A02/A03. These are direct consequences of A02 (and partially A03) disappearing. The DIR002 shows A03's outgoing changed: A02 edge gone (A02 no longer exists), new edges to A05/A07/A10/A11 appear.

Hmm, but are the A03/A14 decreases part of the main hypothesis? They could be a separate difference: A03 and A14 participation dropped from ~49% to ~19%. That's a distinct behavioural difference (reduced participation of A03 and A14). The routing shifts (A08→A03 instead of A10, A09→A10 instead of A03, A14→A13, A15→A10) suggest a rerouting around A03/A14 towards A10/A13/A07.

Actually, let me think about whether there's a coherent single hypothesis: "A02 disappeared, and the paths through A03 and A14 became much rarer, with traffic shifting to A10 and A13." That could be one structural change: a block of activities (A02, and partially A03/A14) was removed/bypassed, with flow redirected to A10/A13/A07/A11.

But the instructions warn: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows... It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window..." Here A02 is absent in the later window, so the path-frequency-shift framing doesn't apply. Instead this is "activities were added or removed, became optional or mandatory" territory.

So the main hypothesis: A02 was removed (no longer observed in any trace), i.e., part of the process is no longer executed. This is directly supported.

Secondary differences: A03 and A14 participation roughly halved (49% → 19%), occur later in traces; A10 participation nearly doubled (24% → 46%) and occurs earlier; multiple routing profiles redistributed (A08 now mostly to A03, A09 now mostly to A10, A14 now mostly to A13, A15 now mostly to A10, A10's outgoing shifted from A02/A13 to A07/A11); several activity pairs changed from usually co-occurring to rarely co-occurring (A03/A13, A03/A14, A13/A14, A07/A14, A09/A14) and others from rarely to usually co-occurring (A07/A10, A09/A10, A10/A13).

Are the A03/A14 decreases and A10 increase part of the main hypothesis or "other differences"? The main hypothesis is about A02's removal. The A03/A14/A10 changes are separate participation changes. I could frame the main hypothesis more broadly: "the paths through A02 (and partly A03/A14) were removed, with flow redirected to A10" — but that risks over-merging. The instruction says "Several indicators and activities can reflect the same trace behaviour; agreeing items are not automatically independent confirmations." The A02 items (OCC001, DIR001, POS001, REL001–009) all reflect one behaviour: A02 vanished.

I think the cleanest: Main hypothesis = A02 is no longer executed/observed (removed from the process). Supported level? Let's weigh.

Support level decision: The count gate passes (60 vs 0.67). Directness: OCC001 is direct evidence of participation change. Consistency: DIR001, POS001, REL001–009 all consistent. Competing explanations: chance sampling — with 97/200 traces containing A02 before, zero in 200 after is essentially impossible by chance; empirical strength 0.995 for all items. The main competing explanation that can't be ruled out: A02 might have been renamed/relabelled rather than removed — but we shouldn't speculate about that? Actually mentioning a competing explanation is required: "Briefly mention an important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out." For disappearance, the competing explanation is that A02 still occurs but was not captured/labelled in the later window (e.g., renamed), or that the later window sample somehow excludes it — but with 200 traces and prior 48.5% participation, random sampling is ruled out. Relabelling can't be ruled out from this evidence. Hmm, but is relabelling a "competing explanation" worth mentioning? The instruction says don't speculate about causes/intentions/labels... "do not speculate about causes, intentions, business events, benchmark labels, change pattern names or drift types." Relabelling would be speculation about labels. Maybe better competing explanation: we cannot distinguish "A02 removed entirely" from "A02 became conditional in a sub-population no longer present in the sample" — hmm, that's basically the same.

Alternatively, frame the main hypothesis as: "part of the process involving A02 is no longer executed (A02 not observed in any later-window trace), and flows that previously passed through A02 now reach their successors directly or via other activities." The competing explanation: the evidence cannot show whether A02 was removed or whether the later window's cases simply never required it — but with 0/200 vs 97/200, that's implausible... Actually "zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window" — the instruction explicitly tempers this. So the competing explanation: A02 could still exist in the process but be triggered only by case types absent from the later sample. That's a fair competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out.

Now, is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence for A02's disappearance is direct (OCC + DIR + POS + REL all consistent), the change is from common to completely absent with large support (97 traces before, 0 after out of 200 each). The screening count is 60 vs 0.67 expected — massively more than chance. I'd say "Supported hypothesis" for the A02 removal. The rerouting changes (A03/A14 down, A10 up) are consistent and directly measured too (OCC002, OCC003, POS002, POS003, POS005, DIR items, REL items). 

But should the main hypothesis include the A03/A14/A10 shifts? The instruction: "State one main hypothesis first and name the activities it involves and how their behaviour changed." A hypothesis like "the process was restructured: A02 disappeared and flow was rerouted from A03/A14 to A10/A13" involves multiple activities. The evidence: A02 disappearance (direct), A03/A14 participation halved (direct), A10 participation doubled (direct), routing shifts (direct DIR measurements). These are all direct participation/routing changes. Together they suggest a structural change: a segment containing A02 was removed and traffic redirected.

However, caution: "Several indicators and activities can reflect the same trace behaviour; agreeing items are not automatically independent confirmations." The A03/A14 changes are distinct from A02's disappearance (different activities). But they could be one underlying change (e.g., a path A02→A03→A14 removed). We can't verify the exact structure, but we can describe: A02 no longer observed; A03 and A14 much rarer; A10 more common and earlier; many successor profiles redistributed.

I think a defensible main hypothesis: "A02 was removed from the observed process (executed in about 49 in 100 traces before, 0 after), and the flows through A03 and A14 became much less frequent while A10 became more frequent — consistent with a structural change that removed a segment around A02 and shifted work to A10." Hmm, but combining might overreach. The instruction says if evidence shows other differences not part of the hypothesis, report under "Other differences:". 

Option A: Main hypothesis = A02 removal only. Other differences = A03/A14 decrease, A10 increase, routing redistributions, lag shifts.

Option B: Main hypothesis = structural change removing A02 and rerouting flow (A03/A14 down, A10 up). Other = lag distribution shifts.

I lean toward Option A being safer but Option B being more informative. Actually, the DIR evidence directly shows rerouting: e.g., A08's outgoing went from 81% A10 to 69% A03; A09's from 35% A03 to 47% A10; A14's from 33% A07 to 76% A13; A15's from 60% A03 to 63% A10. These are direct successor changes. The participation changes of A03/A14/A10 are direct. So a hypothesis "the routing around A02/A03/A14 was restructured, with A10 taking a larger role" is supported by direct evidence.

But is it one hypothesis or several? The A02 disappearance is the clearest single change. The A03/A14 decrease and A10 increase are participation changes in their own right. The DIR redistributions are routing changes. They're plausibly all facets of one structural change, but the evidence doesn't prove they're one change. The instruction: "state one main hypothesis first and name the activities it involves and how their behaviour changed. If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards."

I'll frame the main hypothesis as: A02 is no longer executed (removed from the process), and consequently flows that used to pass through A02 were rerouted — with A03 and A14 also much less frequently executed and A10 taking a larger, earlier role. Hmm, "consequently" is causal speculation. Avoid.

Better: Main hypothesis: a structural change removed A02 from the observed behaviour and made A03 and A14 far less frequent, while A10 became more frequent and appears earlier; routing into/out of these activities was redistributed (A08 now mostly leads to A03 instead of A10; A09 and A15 now mostly lead to A10 instead of A03; A14 now mostly leads to A13). That's a lot for one hypothesis. Maybe split:

Main hypothesis: A02 was removed from the process — it appeared in about 49 in 100 traces before (mean ~1 per trace) and in 0 of 200 traces after; all its outgoing transitions and co-occurrences vanished. Supporting signs: OCC001, DIR001, POS001, REL001–REL009. If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:' without adding their activities to the main hypothesis."

The A03/A14 decrease and A10 increase are clearly part of the same overall behavioural shift, but whether they're "part of this hypothesis" depends on how I define the hypothesis. If the hypothesis is "A02 was removed", then the A03/A14/A10 changes are other differences. If the hypothesis is "the process was restructured around removing the A02/A03/A14 segment with A10 gaining", then they're part of it.

Given the strong interconnection (REL items show A03's co-occurrences dropping, DIR shows rerouting away from A03/A14 toward A10/A13), I could define the main hypothesis as: "The paths through A02, and to a lesser extent A03 and A14, were removed or made far rarer, with flow redirected towards A10 and A13." Main hypothesis (Supported): A02 is no longer executed in the observed process — participation fell from about 49 in 100 traces (mean ~1 occurrence per trace) to 0 in 200 traces, its outgoing transitions vanished, and nine activity pairs involving A02 changed from regularly co-occurring to never co-occurring. So the main hypothesis can involve multiple activities. I'll make the main hypothesis: "A structural change removed A02 from execution and made A03 and A14 much rarer, redirecting flow towards A10 (and A13/A07/A11)." Supporting signs: direct participation drops for A02 (0/200), A03, A14; participation rise for A10; DIR redistributions consistent (successors away from A02/A03/A14 towards A10/A13); REL co-occurrence changes consistent.
